assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general, tractable framework for how a sender's choice of information structure shapes decisions. They extend the information-economics line recognised in earlier prizes. The work is rigorous and has reached theory, mechanism design, regulation, platforms and applied settings.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated the persuasion model. Morris is central to the Bayes-correlated-equilibrium and robust information-design programme, and also to global games and robust mechanism design. Bergemann is a close co-contributor on the same programme, so a three-name limit leaves out a defensible fourth contributor.
assessment.maturity: The founding paper dates from 2011 and the field has developed over roughly 15 years. Theory, empirical use and policy applications have had time to accumulate and be checked.
uncertainties: Choosing among Kamenica, Gentzkow, Morris and Bergemann is contestable, and Gentzkow's other work is largely outside this discovery.
Field and policy applications are still growing, so empirical impact is less established than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm model changed trade theory by explaining selection into exporting and the within-industry reallocation behind the gains from trade. It also established a measurable micro-foundation that reshaped both empirical and quantitative work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core contribution. Helpman's work on firm heterogeneity, FDI and later empirical extensions is a sizeable complement. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are major contributors to the same literature but are not in this candidate's credited names, so credit is partly incomplete.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation, extension and quantitative use give strong evidence of durability, even though some predictions have been refined or qualified.
uncertainties: Credit is shared with scholars outside the credited list.
Helpman may be seen as better credited under a broader trade-theory recognition, and Redding is a plausible alternative third name.
Some of the model's stylised predictions are debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, built on nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and interest-rate rules, underlies modern monetary-policy analysis in central banks worldwide. It has substantial scientific and practical influence.
assessment.attribution: Taylor (staggered contracts, the Taylor rule), Calvo (time-dependent pricing) and Woodford (the microfounded synthesis of the framework) cover the core. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets contributed materially, so the three-name limit forces a hard choice and risks under-crediting.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and refinement, including stress from the financial crisis and the 2021-23 inflation episode. The framework has proven durable and adaptable.
uncertainties: Attribution is diffuse across at least eight credited names.
Critiques after 2008 and 2021-23 concern the framework's adequacy for financial frictions and for inflation dynamics.
Taylor and Calvo's key contributions are older than the synthesis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: GMM estimators for dynamic panels are standard tools across applied microeconomics, macroeconomics and finance. They solved a core identification problem, lagged dependent variables with fixed effects, in a form researchers could use directly. The Nobel prize has recognised methodological contributions of this kind.
assessment.attribution: Arellano-Bond (1991) and Arellano-Bover and Blundell-Bond (1995, 1998) form a clear core. Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen, Anderson-Hsiao and Hansen's GMM are key antecedents, and Hansen already holds a prize. Blundell is also credited on other work, so the discovery-specific contribution should be separated from his broader record.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of very heavy use. Weak-instrument and many-instruments problems are well documented and have not diminished the methods' standing.
uncertainties: The methods are widely used but are sometimes applied mechanically, and instrument proliferation is a recognised concern.
Antecedent work on which the estimators build complicates credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining gave a strategic foundation for bargaining outcomes, and the decentralised-market extension linked bargaining to search and price formation. It is a pillar of modern theory used in labour, industrial organisation, finance, and monetary and market models.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the central originator, and Rubinstein-Wolinsky (1985) is the key market extension. Binmore's contributions, notably the Binmore-Rubinstein-Wolinsky 1986 link to the Nash solution, are important but a smaller share. Stahl, Sutton and Nash's earlier bargaining work are relevant context.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of deep and stable influence. The core results are robust and the work is canonical, though much of the field's recognition has already arrived through its use.
uncertainties: Some of the work is more foundational and theoretical than directly empirically confirmed.
The prize has already recognised nearby theory (for example Nash, Harsanyi and Selten, and mechanism design), which may affect relative priority.
Binmore's share of credit is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a tractable way to quantify how frictions across firms lower aggregate TFP, helping explain cross-country income differences. It has influenced development and growth research and policy discussions.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) and Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) are the main sources. Restuccia is credited here, but Richard Rogerson is not on the list, so credit assignment is incomplete. The measurement approach also draws on earlier work.
assessment.maturity: Some 15 years of use. Its measurement basis has been challenged and refined, which suggests a lasting contribution but with unsettled magnitudes.
uncertainties: Measurement error and the interpretation of dispersion in marginal products as distortions are contested.
Rogerson's absence from the credited names complicates attribution.
Recent enough that long-run assessment is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework for technology and the China-trade-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour-market polarisation, regional adjustment and the distributional costs of trade and technology. The empirical work has had substantial policy and public influence.
assessment.attribution: Autor-Levy-Murnane and Autor-Katz on tasks and skill-biased change, and Autor-Dorn-Hanson on the China shock, are central. Acemoglu (already a laureate) and Restrepo overlap on task models. Katz is also credited elsewhere, and the task and trade-shock contributions have partly different authorship, which makes a three-name set imperfect.
assessment.maturity: The task framework is established, while the China-shock results are still being refined with debate about identification and long-run effects.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior laureate Acemoglu's work on technology and inequality.
Disagreement about the persistence and external validity of the China-shock estimates.
Combining two partly distinct contributions complicates proposed laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of reciprocity and inequity aversion, supported by experiments, explained patterns in ultimatum, public-goods and contract settings that standard self-interest could not. They influenced behavioural contract theory, cooperation, and the economics of norms and enforcement.
assessment.attribution: Fehr-Schmidt (1999) is the formal inequity-aversion model, and Fehr's wider experimental programme (including with Gächter and Falk) is the empirical backbone. Bolton-Ockenfels (2000) is a closely competing model not in the credited names, which affects credit. Rabin's reciprocity model is credited elsewhere on the list.
assessment.maturity: Some 25 years of replication, extension and use, including field evidence. The conceptual contribution is established, though the model's specific functional form has competitors.
uncertainties: Competing models and the absence of Bolton-Ockenfels and Rabin from this set complicate attribution.
The external validity of laboratory social-preference findings and the stability of preference parameters are debated.
Behavioural economics has already been recognised several times, which may affect priority.
